ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TRENGGALEK REGENCY

NUMBER 10 OF 2012

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of human rights of women and children still cannot encourage them to become a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. 40 - Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors of the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of complete, comprehensive, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. 41 - In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize such integrity and harmony, it is very dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Trenggalek Regency.

7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or threat of violence.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully.

10. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

12. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of abuse and neglect.

REGENT OF TRENGGALEK,

Considering:
a. that the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees the welfare of each of its citizens, including protection of women's rights and children's rights which are human rights; b. that in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women is an effort to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life; c. that every child is a bud, potential, and successor generation of the nation's struggle, and is expected to be able to bear that responsibility in the future, therefore they need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally and socially, and have noble character, so that protection efforts need to be made and to realize child welfare by providing guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and the existence of treatment without discrimination; d. that violence against women and children is a crime against humanity which constitutes a violation of human rights; 2 -
e. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, letter c, and letter d, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children; In View of:

The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence.

Article 4

The objectives of implementing child protection are: a. to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity;
b. to protect children and prevent all forms of violence and discrimination against children; andc. to realize children who are qualified, of noble character, and prosperous.

Article 51

1. Special protection for children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 44 is the obligation and responsibility of the Regional Government and the community.
2. Special protection for children who are exploited as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through: a. dissemination and/or socialization of provisions of Laws and Regulations related to the protection of children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and c. involvement of various Regional Government agencies, companies, labor unions, Community Social Institutions, and the community in the elimination of exploitation of children economically and/or sexually.
3. Every person is prohibited from placing, allowing, committing, ordering to commit, or participating in committing exploitation of children as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 44

Regional Governments and other state institutions are obliged and responsible for providing special protection to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (napza) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.

CHAPTER V

PROTECTION OF VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Part One

Rights of Victims

Article 12

1. Every child who is deprived of liberty has the right to: a. receive humane treatment and be placed separately from adults;
b. obtain legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal proceedings; andc. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial children's court in a hearing closed to the public.
2. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.

Article 62

Regional Government is obliged to implement prevention of acts of violence, criminal acts of trafficking in persons, and protection efforts for victims.

The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of human rights of women and children still cannot encourage them to become a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. 40 - Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors of the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence.

NUMBER 10 OF 2012

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of human rights of women and children still cannot encourage them to become a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. 40 - Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors of the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of complete, comprehensive, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. 41 - In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize such integrity and harmony, it is very dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of human rights of women and children still cannot encourage them to become a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. 40 - Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors of the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of complete, comprehensive, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. 41 - In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize such integrity and harmony, it is very dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of human rights of women and children still cannot encourage them to become a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. 40 - Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors of the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of complete, comprehensive, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. 41 - In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize such integrity and harmony, it is very dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence.

REGENT OF TRENGGALEK,

Considering:
a. that the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees the welfare of each of its citizens, including protection of women's rights and children's rights which are human rights; b. that in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women is an effort to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life; c. that every child is a bud, potential, and successor generation of the nation's struggle, and is expected to be able to bear that responsibility in the future, therefore they need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally and socially, and have noble character, so that protection efforts need to be made and to realize child welfare by providing guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and the existence of treatment without discrimination; d. that violence against women and children is a crime against humanity which constitutes a violation of human rights; 2 -

Paragraph 1

General

The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence.

a. that the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees the welfare of each of its citizens, including protection of women's rights and children's rights which are human rights; b. that in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women is an effort to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life; c. that every child is a bud, potential, and successor generation of the nation's struggle, and is expected to be able to bear that responsibility in the future, therefore they need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally and socially, and have noble character, so that protection efforts need to be made and to realize child welfare by providing guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and the existence of treatment without discrimination; d. that violence against women and children is a crime against humanity which constitutes a violation of human rights; 2 -

The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of human rights of women and children still cannot encourage them to become a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. 40 - Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors of the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of complete, comprehensive, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. 41 - In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize such integrity and harmony, it is very dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of human rights of women and children still cannot encourage them to become a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. 40 - Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors of the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of complete, comprehensive, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. 41 - In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize such integrity and harmony, it is very dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of human rights of women and children still cannot encourage them to become a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. 40 - Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors of the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of complete, comprehensive, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. 41 - In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize such integrity and harmony, it is very dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence.

ON

NUMBER 10 OF 2012

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that side with vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, becomes very necessary in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of human rights of women and children still cannot encourage them to become a political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of protection of women carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. 40 - Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of such obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors of the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of complete, comprehensive, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. 41 - In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on the Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize such integrity and harmony, it is very dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. The integrity and harmony of the household can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination.

Regional Government is obliged and responsible to provide support for facilities and infrastructure in the implementation of child protection.

Article 44

Regional Governments and other state institutions are obliged and responsible for providing special protection to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance (napza) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.

b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and c. involvement of various Regional Government agencies, companies, labor unions, Community Social Institutions, and the community in the elimination of exploitation of children economically and/or sexually.
3. Every person is prohibited from placing, allowing, committing, ordering to commit, or participating in committing exploitation of children as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 1

Article 22

1. Regional Government guarantees the protection, maintenance, and welfare of children with due regard to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, or other persons legally responsible for the child.
2. Regional Government supervises the implementation of child protection.

The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence.

The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates matters of prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates matters of obligations for law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence.
